claims.text: The initial Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy is a single-phase BCC material.
Dendritic/interdendritic micro-segregation causes asymmetric XRD peaks in the initial alloy.
The baseline alloy's low fracture strain is caused by micro-segregation and the lack of secondary-phase reinforcement.
Adding approximately 4 at.% Cr to Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr will induce a complex multicomponent Laves phase.
The Cr-induced Laves phase will have a volume fraction of approximately 4%.
The Laves phase may have a composition such as (Hf,Mo,Ta,Zr)2Cr.
The proposed composition and processing route will favor a reticulated or interconnected Laves-phase morphology.
The reticulated Laves phase will occur within interdendritic regions.
A reticulated Laves-phase morphology will deflect or bridge cracks and create a tortuous crack path.
Crack deflection and bridging by the Laves phase will impede crack extension and increase fracture strain.
Atomic-size mismatch from Cr solute atoms will produce significant lattice distortion in the BCC matrix.
Cr-induced lattice distortion will increase Peierls stress and provide solid-solution hardening.
Cr addition will contract the BCC lattice because Cr has a smaller atomic radius than Hf and Zr.
The expected BCC lattice-parameter contraction is approximately 0.005–0.010 Å.
BCC lattice contraction will shift the corresponding XRD peaks to higher 2θ.
High-resolution synchrotron XRD with Rietveld refinement can separate segregation-related asymmetric broadening, matrix peak shifts, and distinct Laves-phase peaks.
Cr addition will significantly increase fracture strain relative to the Cr-free baseline.
Cr-induced solid-solution hardening will increase yield strength.
Keeping the Laves-phase fraction near 4% will avoid embrittlement, whereas fractions above 10–15% may make the alloy brittle.
The cited study reports Laves-phase formation in a different CrMoNbWV refractory alloy system.
